strings.name: Patricia Urquiola
strings.summary: Patricia Urquiola is a Spanish-born architect and designer working in Milan, with a practice spanning furniture, interiors and exhibition installations. She co-founded her studio with Alberto Zontone and has served as Cassina’s art director since 2015. Her designs combine materials, color, craft and industrial production.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Cofounders, manufacturers and curatorial partners retain credit. Material experiments do not establish independently verified environmental benefits. Plans for 2027 are not completed projects.
strings.influence.rationale: Combines craft and industrial production through furniture, materials and interior design, advancing experience and form in international product design.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Studied architecture in Madrid before graduating from the Politecnico di Milano in 1989 under Achille Castiglioni.
strings.facts.f2.label: Design in museum collections
strings.facts.f2.value: MoMA holds her 2002 Fjord Armchair and Foot Stool, manufactured by Moroso; collection status does not mean currently on display.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Furniture and spatial design
strings.highlights.h1.text: From Fjord seating to exhibition spaces, her multidisciplinary practice encompasses product design, architecture and art direction.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Material and interactive experiments
strings.highlights.h2.text: The 2026 among-all installation combined textiles and interactive AI; Meta-morphosa presented the studio’s recent material research.
strings.timeline.t1.title: NeoCon projects and the Sosu collection
strings.timeline.t1.text: Haworth announces Sosu sofas and tables; she designs the showroom installation and curates DesignLab with Paved States.
strings.timeline.t2.title: among-all in Frankfurt
strings.timeline.t2.text: Introduces the textile and interactive AI installation at Heimtextil’s opening press conference, within the context of the fair and its collaborating teams.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Meta-morphosa opens
strings.timeline.t3.text: She co-curates the CID exhibition at Grand-Hornu with Marie Pok; it runs through April 26, 2026.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Becomes Cassina art director
strings.timeline.t4.text: Takes responsibility for art direction; the role is not the company’s chief executive position.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Fjord Armchair and Foot Stool
strings.timeline.t5.text: Designs the furniture for Moroso; MoMA’s record credits designer and manufacturer separately.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Co-founds the studio
strings.timeline.t6.text: Founds Studio Urquiola with Alberto Zontone, working on products, architecture and installations.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Leads the Lissoni design group
strings.timeline.t7.text: Her studio biography dates her appointment as head of Lissoni Associati’s design group to this year.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Graduates in architecture in Milan
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes her studies at the Politecnico di Milano under Achille Castiglioni, having previously studied in Madrid.
